At more than 5 s old, a live pointing says Pointing stale in the existing solved-time clause and guidance lines, with no turn or tilt. The 250 ms timer uses console time from polls and live events. components.name: Scope Node and Camera
components.description: Built in ScopeNodeSection.tsx on /setup. Shows link state and camera model from session reads, and latest star count from live events. Ruled 44px address and empty password token fields; token_set says A token is set, blank preserves it, successful save clears it. Exposure and gain take auto or a positive value; threshold takes 1–50 sigma or auto for 8 sigma. One PUT saves the entered fields. Stored exposure/gain outside the camera range names the value and range. FieldWarning.tsx shows solved field beside database range, warning within 1 degree of an end, outside it, or after 30 s unsolved with at least 10 stars. Drafts survive live events; refusals use ink alerts.

components.name: Aim-Point Tap
components.description: Built in AimTap.tsx on /setup. Centre a star in the eyepiece, then tap the .photo live preview. The shown photograph retains its frame id and full-frame dimensions; a tap scales its displayed rectangle to full-frame pixels and POSTs /api/aim. The console snaps to a star. 422 and expired-frame reasons stay visible without changing the aim point. Unloaded or failed previews accept no tap. Saved coordinates and Reset aim point remain available without a preview; DELETE restores frame centre immediately. Moving the finder camera is the cue to reset. Existing ink and red-only filter at night.

Aim point

components.name: GoTo
components.description: Built in GoToControl.tsx inside GuidanceBlock. Present with mount telemetry; enabled only for a connected mount, no running GoTo or second sync, and no server goto_refusal. The exact planner refusal is printed and linked with aria-describedby. A primary 44px button POSTs /api/goto. An ink status shows Slewing, Solving, each numbered Correction and On target with the final error to 0.1 arcsecond, or the halt/failure reason. Motion requests refresh immediately and mount sessions poll every 500ms, waiting for an outstanding read to finish. Existing dim primary and red-only night tokens.
components.html: Correction 1 · On target · 12.3″

components.name: Stop
components.description: Built in StopButton.tsx in the sticky TopBar shared by console and Setup. Visible whenever mount.moving or a GoTo/second sync is slewing, solving or correcting. With a connected mount, Track states armed, tracking and keyhole_wait also keep Stop visible on every page, including Setup, while axes rest before autonomous motion. Absent or ended Track adds no Stop. No mount telemetry renders nothing. Always enabled, including pending, failed and repeated bodyless POST /api/stop requests. Explicit 44px minimum height, square ink border, red-only night tokens. With a mount, target and frame sheets are nonmodal dialogs fixed below the top bar (4rem inset, layer 20 below 30); Stop stays outside every dialog and inert/aria-hidden subtree. Close and Escape dismiss the sheets. Mount top-bar gaps tighten to 4px on phones; below 380px the site chip yields to Stop and remains available in Setup. Fits at 320px.
components.html: <header class="ds-motion-bar"><button class="ds-stop">Stop</button></header>

components.name: Mount and Pointing Model
components.description: Built in MountSection.tsx on Setup below Scope node and camera. Four parts: link state, scope address, board (or Board not reported) and reported firmware; base tilt to 0.1 degree toward whole-degree azimuth; RMS residual to 0.1 arcsecond and sync count; Second sync and resets for the night model and fixed terms. An unfitted tilt explains two syncs at least 90 degrees apart. Second sync POSTs /api/model/second-sync; each reset POSTs /api/model/reset with what night or fixed. Model actions disable while pending or moving; top-bar Stop stays enabled. Hairline rules, square 44px controls, ink successes/refusals and existing red-only night tokens.

components.name: Track and Tracking Readout
components.description: Built in TrackControl.tsx beside GoTo inside GuidanceBlock. Only a connected mount offers the labelled Track Switch; POST /api/track sends on and refreshes the session. Server wanted/state drive the switch. Ink statuses name the target, armed wait for GoTo and keyhole wait. Endings stay in the Track region: observer Stop, link lost, Sun up, target too low or the server GoTo reason. The readout gives last-minute RMS error to 1 arcsecond, field rotation to 0.01°/min and, with an imaging camera, longest exposure for 1 px corner smear to 0.1 s or no limit. Wrapping tabular figures, Second Ink labels and red-only night tokens. No mount adds no height.

components.name: Imaging Camera
components.description: Built in ImagingCameraSection.tsx on Setup below Mount and pointing model. Two-column Sensor width and Sensor height fields in mm and Pixel pitch in µm, labelled square 44px transparent inputs with trailing Second Ink units and 2px focus outlines. Save imaging camera PUTs imaging_camera; Forget imaging camera sends null. Finite dimensions must be greater than 0 and at most 100 mm, pitch greater than 0 and at most 50 µm. Invalid values save nothing and print the allowed ranges in an ink alert; standing range help is linked to the fields. Drafts survive polls, save errors stay visible, and returning to guidance after saving gains the exposure readout. Hairline rules and existing red-only night tokens.

narrative.overview:
The console is an atlas chart of the observer's own frame. The solve proves itself by drawing the sky's RA/Dec graticule and the atlas's deep-sky symbols over the real photograph, labelled at the edges in a paper margin the way a printed star atlas labels a chart. Everything around the chart is set like the atlas's own furniture: a double-ruled title block, hairline rules between entries, square ruled boxes for controls, black ink on cool paper.

The system ships in two editions of the same chart. The day edition is the desk edition: cool paper, near-black ink in three strengths, hairline rules, and the atlas's object colours (green nebulae, gold clusters, red galaxies) kept to object symbols and labels. The night edition is the field edition read under a red torch: black ground and red ink in three brightnesses, every token on the red channel alone, and photographs passed through a luminance-to-red filter so not one white pixel reaches the screen. Density is that of a reference chart: dense facts, tabular figures, few surfaces, no decoration. The confirmed rejection is the planetarium-app default of navy glass cards, cyan glow and starfield wallpaper.
keyCharacteristics: An RA/Dec graticule and atlas symbols drawn over the real frame are the signature.
Square ruled boxes in 1px ink; the only rounded thing is the dialog sheet.
Flat: no shadows anywhere; depth is rule weight and tone.
One family, Archivo Variable, worked through its width axis and italic.
Two editions from one token set: day paper and ink, night red on black.

rules.name: The Objects-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, gold and red belong to deep-sky objects. Chrome, controls and text stay in ink.

rules.name: The Red Torch Rule
rules.body: At night every pixel is red or black: no white, no other hue, and no token brighter than Night Ink. Anything new, images and embedded views included, must take a night token or the red-only filter before it ships.

rules.name: The Dim Primary Rule
rules.body: At night the primary button is a Night Rule block with Night Ink text, never a solid Night Ink fill. A full-ink block would be the brightest thing on screen.

rules.name: The Italic Object Rule
rules.body: Deep-sky object identifiers are always italic, on the chart and in lists. Star names stay upright.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: `tnum` is on for the whole body. Coordinates, magnitudes and counts line up in columns.

rules.name: The Neatline Rule
rules.body: If something needs separation, rule it. Use 1px ink for a box, the doubled rule for the title block, and the hairline between rows. Never a shadow, never a tinted card.

dos: **Do** draw new chart content as atlas furniture: 1px or chart-unit strokes, currentColor, cased labels, edge labels in the paper margin.
**Do** give every new colour a night value on the red channel no brighter than Night Ink (`#e00000`), and put every new raster or embedded view under the `.photo` red-only filter.
**Do** separate with rules: a 1px ink box for controls, the doubled 3px-gap rule for a title block, hairlines between rows.
**Do** set object IDs in italic and keep figures tabular.
**Do** keep controls square and at least 44px (38px for chips) tall.
**Do** use the expo-out curve (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) at 160 to 280ms for state changes, with every animation removed under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use navy glass cards, cyan glow or starfield wallpaper.
**Don't** show a white or non-red pixel in night mode, including in images, previews, embedded views and the first paint.
**Don't** use the nebula, cluster or galaxy colours on chrome, controls or text that is not an object.
**Don't** use a box-shadow, or round a control's corners.
**Don't** fill a night control with solid Night Ink.
